title: Move sessions out of process memory
summary: Sessions live in a `Map` inside each API process, so every deploy logs everyone out and the second replica can't see the first one's logins. I want to move them to a shared store with a 30-day sliding expiry. **I need two decisions from you before I start:** where sessions should live, and whether users can see and revoke their other sessions.
status: Plan ready. I haven't changed any code yet.

blocks.title: What I'm assuming
blocks.note: Mark anything wrong. These change the plan.

items.text: We run exactly two API replicas behind a load balancer with no sticky sessions.
Postgres 15 is already in production and the API has a connection pool to it.
Logging everyone out once, on the deploy that ships this, is acceptable.

blocks.title: Where sessions live
blocks.question: Which store should back sessions?
blocks.context: Roughly 4k active sessions, ~40 auth checks per second at peak. Hard to undo: switching stores later means another forced logout.

options.label: Postgres table
options.summary: A `sessions` table with an index on `expires_at`, swept hourly.
cons: One extra query per request (≈1 ms on our pool)
options.evidence: Spiked on a scratch branch against a copy of prod data: the extra query adds **1.1 ms** at p95 on our existing pool.

options.label: Redis
cons: New service to run, back up and monitor
options.evidence: Spiked with a local Redis 7: **0.4 ms** at p95, but it needs a new client, a health check and a backup plan.

options.label: Signed cookie, no server store
options.summary: Put the session in an encrypted cookie.
cons: Can't revoke a session before it expires

blocks.title: Risk
blocks.body: Everyone is logged out once when this deploys, because the in-memory sessions can't be migrated. I'd ship it at a quiet hour and post a notice first.
